description:
Atma Nirbhar Krishi Yojana is a significant initiative launched by the Government of India to promote self-reliance in the agricultural sector. 

The scheme was officially launched on May 15, 2020. 

It was introduced as part of the broader Atma Nirbhar Bharat Abhiyan, which translates to Self-Reliant India Movement. 

The primary objective of the Atma Nirbhar Krishi Yojana is to enhance the income of farmers and promote sustainable agricultural practices. 

The scheme aims to provide financial assistance and support to farmers to improve productivity and ensure food security. 

One of the measurable targets of the scheme is to increase the income of farmers by 1.5 times by the year 2022. 

The scheme also aims to promote the adoption of modern agricultural technologies and practices. 

Under this initiative, the government has allocated a budget of ₹1 lakh crore for the development of agricultural infrastructure. 

This budget is intended to improve supply chains and create a more robust agricultural ecosystem. 

The benefits of the Atma Nirbhar Krishi Yojana include direct financial assistance to farmers. 

Farmers can receive up to ₹2 lakh as a loan under this scheme. 

The interest subsidy provided under this scheme can be as high as 3 percent. 

Additionally, the scheme encourages the establishment of Farmer Producer Organizations (FPOs). 

FPOs can help farmers gain better access to markets and improve their bargaining power. 

The eligibility criteria for the Atma Nirbhar Krishi Yojana include being a farmer or a member of a farmer's family. 

There are no specific age limits for eligibility. 

However, it is essential for applicants to have a valid land ownership document. 

Farmers must also possess a bank account to facilitate the disbursement of funds. 

The application process for the Atma Nirbhar Krishi Yojana is straightforward. 

Farmers need to visit the official website of the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers' Welfare. 

They must fill out the application form available online. 

Required documents include proof of land ownership and identity verification documents. 

Farmers may also need to provide their bank account details for fund transfer. 

Once the application is submitted, it is reviewed by the concerned authorities. 

The timeline for application processing can vary but typically takes about 15 to 30 days. 

Disbursement of funds is done directly to the farmer's bank account. 

The frequency of assistance under this scheme is determined based on the specific needs of the farmers. 

The implementing authority for the Atma Nirbhar Krishi Yojana is the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers' Welfare. 

The Ministry has various departments that oversee the implementation of this scheme at the state and district levels. 

Farmers can contact the Ministry through their official helpline number, which is 1800 180 1551. 

The scheme also emphasizes the importance of technology in agriculture. 

Farmers are encouraged to adopt digital platforms for better access to information and resources. 

The government has partnered with various organizations to provide training and support to farmers. 

These organizations help in skill development and capacity building. 

The Atma Nirbhar Krishi Yojana also focuses on promoting organic farming practices. 

Farmers are encouraged to shift towards sustainable agricultural practices. 

This includes the use of organic fertilizers and pest control methods. 

The government has set a target to increase the area under organic farming to 2 million hectares by 2025. 

The scheme also aims to improve irrigation facilities across the country. 

The government plans to enhance irrigation coverage to 100 percent by 2022. 

This includes the construction of new irrigation projects and the renovation of existing ones. 

The Atma Nirbhar Krishi Yojana also promotes the use of renewable energy in agriculture. 

Farmers are encouraged to use solar panels and wind energy for irrigation and other agricultural activities. 

The government has set aside ₹10,000 crore for renewable energy projects in agriculture. 

The scheme also supports the development of agricultural markets. 

This includes the establishment of modern market yards and cold storage facilities. 

The government aims to create 10,000 new FPOs by 2024. 

These FPOs will provide farmers with better access to resources and markets. 

The Atma Nirbhar Krishi Yojana also emphasizes research and development in agriculture. 

The government has allocated funds for agricultural research institutions to innovate new farming techniques. 

Farmers are encouraged to participate in workshops and training sessions organized by these institutions. 

The scheme also includes provisions for crop insurance. 

Farmers can avail of insurance coverage to protect against crop loss due to natural calamities. 

The government has increased the coverage amount for crop insurance to ₹2 lakh per hectare. 

The Atma Nirbhar Krishi Yojana is a comprehensive approach to transforming the agricultural sector in India. 

It aims to empower farmers and ensure their financial stability. 

The scheme is expected to have a significant impact on rural development and poverty alleviation. 

By promoting self-reliance in agriculture, the government aims to create a sustainable and resilient agricultural ecosystem. 

The Atma Nirbhar Krishi Yojana is a crucial step towards achieving food security in India. 

It aligns with the government's vision of doubling farmers' income and enhancing the overall agricultural productivity. 

Farmers are encouraged to take advantage of this scheme to improve their livelihoods. 

The government continues to monitor and evaluate the progress of the Atma Nirbhar Krishi Yojana. 

Regular assessments are conducted to ensure that the objectives of the scheme are being met. 

The scheme is expected to evolve based on the feedback and needs of the farmers. 

Overall, the Atma Nirbhar Krishi Yojana represents a significant commitment by the Government of India to support its agricultural sector. 

It aims to create a self-sufficient and prosperous farming community across the country.
